header.name: Collaborative Filtering
header.description: Recommender systems have around for sometime. But in recent times with the boom of retail online trade recommendation systems and the hype around the NetFlix competition has made recommender systems a major topic in data mining. In this course we will learn about different aspects of recommender systems with particular emphasis on its algorithms.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate an understanding of concepts of recommender systems.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to implement both primitive (neighbourhood models) and state-of-the-art (latent factor models) algorithms for recommender systems.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to implement advanced projects in this area.

lecture_topics: Explicit vs Implicit Ratings – advantages and disadvantages
Bias Prediction – predicting user and item biases (statistical and optimization based methods)
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Quiz#1: Implementing bias prediction in class

lecture_topics: Rating Prediction – local / neighbourhood models (Including review of some machine learning concepts – clustering, regression, classification)
Rating Prediction – latent factor models / global models (modeling the problem as a matrix completion, theoretical guarantees, algorithms and performances)

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment#3: Implement hybrid model from papers

resources.title: Recommender Systems Handbook, Ricci, F., Rokach, L., Shapira, B., Kantor, P.B. (Eds.), Springer,
Sparse and Redundant Representation: From Theory to Practice, Michael Elad, Springer
